SCOPE-DECISION GATE (§M-2 FHIR operations $viewdefinition-run / -export / $sqlquery-run / -export): Feature Designer MUST surface this as an APPROVAL question for the human. Default recommendation: library-only (fhir4ds does not expose HTTP). If the human chooses server scope, split into a separate feature — do not bundle.

VIEWDEFINITION LAYER GAPS (§G-1..§G-4): §G-1 cnl-1 URL invariant (tighten canonical/URL validators in fhir4ds/viewdef/types.py with _CANONICAL_RE = re.compile(r"^[^|# ]*$"); route ViewDefinition.url, .profile, .meta.profile through it; keep permissive _URI_RE for Column.type. §G-2 cnl-0 name invariant (non-fatal warning from validate_view_definition() when name starts lowercase or exceeds 255 chars — cnl-0 is warning severity, do NOT promote to error). §G-3 CanonicalResource/DomainResource roundtrip via extension-bag: add _extensions: dict[str, Any] catch-all to ViewDefinition dataclass preserving unknown keys verbatim through from_dict/to_dict (defer full-typed-dataclass option A unless a consumer needs it). §G-4 tag namespace (non-fatal warning when column.tag.name lacks a `/` namespace prefix — spec says 'recommended', not 'shall').

MAJOR COMPONENT §M-1 SQLQuery Library profile: DuckDB-only MVP. New fhir4ds/sqlquery/ package mirroring viewdef/ (types, parser, validator, runner). Materialize each relatedArtifact dependency as a DuckDB view (CREATE VIEW "<label>" AS <generated SQL>) so raw SQL in content[].data resolves aliases. Bind parameters via DuckDB prepared statements with FHIR-type->SQL-type coercion — NO string interpolation. Pick application/sql or application/sql;dialect=duckdb content; reject other dialects. Skip AST-level schema validation (spec does not require it). Implement SQLView profile alongside SQLQuery (only diff: parameter 0..0 on SQLView). Estimated 1-2 weeks.

EXTENSION HARDENING (§E-1): joins field, Join dataclass, JoinType enum, JoinGenerator module, and public API exports all STAY. Add clear documentation in viewdef package docstring, Join dataclass docstring, and fhir4ds-private/docs/ that joins is a fhir4ds extension and not part of any past/current SQL-on-FHIR v2 version (reference the §E-1 verification: 1,104 commits searched, 'joins' never appeared in any spec source file). Optional second step (gated on whether any downstream consumer roundtrips ViewDefinitions through other tools): refuse to emit joins in ViewDefinition.to_dict() unless meta.profile declares https://fhir4ds.org/StructureDefinition/JoinExtension.

issues.evidence: `_KNOWN_LIBRARY_KEYS` in `fhir4ds/sqlquery/parser.py` lists `relatedArtifact` twice. Set deduplication makes this functionally harmless, but it suggests the set was assembled hastily and may be missing other Library keys. Cross-check against the FHIR R5 Library resource shape.

`fhir4ds/sqlquery/runner.py` uses lazy imports inside methods (`from .parser import parse_library` in `execute` and `_materialize_one`; `from ..viewdef.generator import SQLGenerator` in `_generate_view_sql`; `from ..viewdef.parser import parse_view_definition` in `_materialize_one`). There is no actual circular import: parser→validator→types+errors; runner is a leaf. The lazy imports appear to be defensive against a future circular that doesn't currently exist, at the cost of readability (each method re-imports on every call).
issues.root_cause: Defensive import style without a concrete cycle to defend against.

issues.evidence: The new `_extensions: Dict[str, Any]` field on `ViewDefinition` (§G-3 extension bag) uses a leading underscore. While Python allows this and the dataclass machinery handles it correctly (field with default, keyword-only by position), leading-underscore dataclass fields are unconventional and may confuse readers who expect `_foo` to mean 'private attribute'. Consider renaming to `extensions_bag` or `unknown_fields` for clarity. The current name was chosen to signal 'not an official FHIR field name' but the same goal can be reached via docstring.
issues.root_cause: Naming choice trading readability for an unneeded privacy signal.

issues.evidence: The cnl-0 warning in `viewdef/parser.py:validate_view_definition()` checks `not vd.name[0].isupper() or len(vd.name) > 255` — flags non-capital or overlong names. The spec regex requires 2-255 chars; single-character names like 'A' technically violate cnl-0 but pass our check. This is documented in the test docstring (`test_single_char_name_warns`) as a conservative non-enforcement of minimum length. Acceptable, but worth surfacing as a known gap.

issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec test `repeat.json:repeat inside forEachOrNull`
issues.evidence: After §G-5 spec suite refresh, this test failed with `Parser Error: syntax error at or near "AND"`. Root cause: `test_spec_compliance.py:_add_resource_type_filter` split on `"\nUNION ALL\n"` without paren-depth awareness, corrupting SQL when UNION ALL appears inside a LATERAL subquery.
issues.root_cause: Test helper used string split on UNION ALL without paren-depth awareness
issues.resolution: Added `_split_top_level_union_all` (string-aware, depth-aware splitter) and `_has_top_level_where` (string-aware, depth-aware WHERE detector) to `test_spec_compliance.py`. Replaced naive regex-based WHERE detection with depth-aware scan.
issues.verified_in: Step 1 §G-5 — 465/465 spec tests pass; 60/60 repeat tests pass

issues.evidence: Three `fn_join.json` tests failed. For Patient p2 (no name), `name.given.join(...)` returned empty FHIRPath collection, but generated SQL produced `''` (empty string) instead of NULL.
issues.root_cause: `fhirpath_text` returns `''` for empty FHIRPath result; column CASE expression had no empty→NULL branch.
issues.resolution: In `generator.py:generate_column_expr`, wrap uncast `fhirpath_text(...)` calls in `NULLIF(..., '')`. TRY_CAST paths already convert empty to NULL via the cast.
issues.verified_in: Step 1 §G-5 — 9/9 fn_join tests pass; no regressions in 2656 viewdef+fhirpath tests

issues.evidence: Two `fn_boundary.json` tests failed. Patient p1 `birthDate: "1970-06"`; column declared `dateTime`. Runtime returned `Date` (since birthDate is a date); `dateTime` compat set excluded `Date`. Type guard rejected.
issues.root_cause: Type compatibility set for `dateTime` excluded `Date` runtime type returned by boundary functions on date inputs.
issues.resolution: Extended `dateTime` compat set to `{DateTime, Date, String, dateTime, date, string}` and symmetrically extended `date` to accept `DateTime`. FHIRPath boundary functions on date inputs legitimately return Date; Date is a strict subtype of DateTime.

issues.evidence: `fn_boundary.json:time highBoundary` failed. Observation o4 `valueTime: "12:34:00"` (seconds precision). Expected `"12:34:00.999"`. Actual: `"12:34:59.999"`. Runtime treated input as minute-precision.
issues.root_cause: `_time_boundary` in `datetime.py` unconditionally used `fill["second"]`, ignoring the input's explicit seconds component.
issues.resolution: Updated `_time_boundary` to preserve input `second` and `ms` when present (match_list[2]/[3]) and only fall back to `fill` values for components below the input's precision. Per FHIRPath, components AT input precision are preserved; components BELOW are boundary-filled.
